newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money steady after initial easing.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money steady after initial easing.

text.p: Dutch money rates headed down at the opening on Friday, but dealers said the slightly easier undertone had disappeared by early afternoon.
They even noted some upward pressure on six-month deposits, but said this was not seen as a trend. Business was thin. "Volumes fizzle out on Fridays," said one dealer.
Dealers said the market had brushed off a bigger than expected Dutch consumer price price, after the statistics office reported a 2.4 percent year-on-year rise in October.
Analysts had forecast a 2.1 percent rise.
Dealers said call money was likely to stay stable for a few more days, since Thursday's allocation of 6.57 billion guilders to the money market was ample.
Call money was trading between 2.62/68 percent bid in afternoon trade, but dealers said some business had been done at 2.56 percent bid earlier.
"There is sufficient liquidity in the market," said one dealer, but he added that overnight money had returned to Thursday's level with banks getting ready for the weekend.
Six-month deposits were bid at 2.98 percent in the afternoon, versus an unchanged 2.94 percent earlier.
The guilder was stable at a slightly lower level against the German mark, at 112.175 per 100 marks versus 112.18 on Thursday.
